# SPE Round 5 plan: invoice extraction

Round 4 had one miss. R predicted 0.95 and measured 0.88. Its Why was "OCR cleanup fixes scanned totals", and that Why broke because the cleanup tool dropped line items on two-column layouts (F9). The 3-rounds-in-a-row stop count goes back to 0. This round tests one fix for F9 and keeps everything else the same.

Defaults I chose where the pasted text left a gap:
- The pasted text does not include the last requirement ID in spec.md. This plan numbers new rows R50 to R55, and I will renumber them to follow on from spec.md when I write the file.
- I read the round 4 log columns as predicted, measured, naive, hit or miss, and closer.
- Round 5 runs 1 trial per invoice. I will match round 4 if round 4 used a different count.

## 1. Specify

### Round 4 proposals

| Proposal | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| P1: keep OCR cleanup but skip it on two-column layouts | Adopt | This is the direct fix for r04 F9. It becomes the only change in new config S. |
| P2: add 15 scanned invoices with handwriting | Reject for round 5 | Q measured 0.93, so it is not at a ceiling. The stop rule calls it a ceiling only when every config hits the maximum. Changing the eval set this round would mix up the P1 result with a new denominator. The AP lead would also need to supply the reference fields, and only the user can arrange that. I am logging it as open decision D-r05-1. |
| P3: drop config P | Adopt | P trails Q on every metric. Q already is P plus one change, so Q becomes the baseline. This removes 60 runs. |

### Configurations

| Config | Definition | One change from |
|---|---|---|
| Q | Sonnet 5.5 with a schema-first prompt (unchanged) | Baseline |
| R | Q with OCR cleanup as a tool (unchanged) | Q |
| S | R, except the agent skips OCR cleanup when the invoice has a two-column line-item layout | R |

I keep R because it measures S against a fresh run of R from the same day. Comparing S to Q tells us whether cleanup helps at all once the two-column damage is removed.

### Requirements (round 5)

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R50 | S matches R except for a rule that skips OCR cleanup on two-column line-item layouts. | P1, r04 F9 | The dry-run config diff shows the skip rule as the only difference between S and R. |
| R51 | On every invoice where R dropped line items in round 4, S extracts the same number of line items as the reference. | r04 F9 | The new `line_item_count` check compares the extracted count to the reference count for each F9 invoice. |
| R52 | The layout check in S reads only the invoice PDF. It never reads reference fields, PO files, or anything under spe/evals/. | Halt rule: leaked answer key | A trace audit of files read during the dry run. |
| R53 | Config P is retired. Q is the baseline. | P3, adopted | The workflow arguments list Q, R, and S only. |
| R54 | The eval set stays the same 60 invoices with the AP lead's reference fields. | Decision: P2 deferred | The grader selftest checks that the eval set hash matches round 4. |
| R55 | The field accuracy grader is unchanged from round 4. | Decision: keep r05 comparable to r04 | Regrading round 4 outputs reproduces Q 0.93 and R 0.88 exactly. |

### Open decisions (add to spe/spec/disagreements.md)

| ID | Question | Option A | Option B | Work affected | Decides | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| D-r05-1 | Should we add 15 scanned handwritten invoices to the eval set? | Add them in round 6 once the AP lead supplies reference fields. | Keep the 60-invoice set. | Eval set, all predictions, grader selftest | User, with the AP lead | Open |

## 2. Predict

Each row starts from round 4's measured value. A number moves only for the reason in its Why. A result is a hit when the measured value falls inside the band. The naive baseline for each cell is its round 4 value. S uses R's value as its naive baseline.

| Metric | Q | R | S | Grader check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Field accuracy (60 invoices) | 0.93 ± 0.02 | 0.88 ± 0.03 | 0.92 ± 0.03 | The round 4 field accuracy check. It does an exact match per field against the AP lead's reference and averages over all invoices. |
| Share of r04 F9 invoices with a dropped line item | 0.05 ± 0.05 | 0.85 ± 0.15 | 0.05 ± 0.05 | The new `line_item_count` check. An invoice counts as dropped when it has fewer extracted line items than the reference. |

Why, by row:
- **Field accuracy.** Q and R did not change, so both stay at their round 4 values. S behaves like Q on two-column invoices and like R on all others, so it should land just under Q. I am withdrawing R's old Why that cleanup fixes scanned totals because round 4 did not prove it. That is why S is not predicted above Q.
- **Dropped line items.** Q never runs cleanup, so it should rarely drop items. R chose these invoices by dropping items on them, but a rerun may vary, so its band is wider. S skips cleanup on these layouts and should match Q.

Diagnostics, reported but not scored: (a) the number of invoices where S skipped cleanup, and (b) Q against S on the total field only. Item (b) tests the withdrawn Why directly.

The draft for `spe/predictions/r05.yaml` looks like this:

```yaml
round: 5
configs: [Q, R, S]
metrics:
  field_accuracy:
    check: field_accuracy_r04
    Q: {predicted: 0.93, band: 0.02, naive: 0.93}
    R: {predicted: 0.88, band: 0.03, naive: 0.88}
    S: {predicted: 0.92, band: 0.03, naive: 0.88}
  f9_dropped_line_items:
    check: line_item_count
    Q: {predicted: 0.05, band: 0.05, naive: 0.05}
    R: {predicted: 0.85, band: 0.15, naive: 1.00}
    S: {predicted: 0.05, band: 0.05, naive: 1.00}
```

## 3. Evaluate

### After approval, before anything runs

1. Save the user's prompt ("go again") and any review corrections, word for word, to `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r05.md`.
2. Add the round 5 requirement table to `spe/spec/spec.md` and mark the "Proposed for round 5" rows as adopted or rejected. Add D-r05-1 to `spe/spec/disagreements.md`.
3. Make a local commit with the subject `spe(r05): specify`.
4. Copy this plan to `spe/plans/r05.md`. Write `spe/predictions/r05.yaml` from the Predict table. Nobody edits that file after a trial runs.
5. Make a local commit with the subject `spe(r05): predict`.

### Build

6. Implement S as a copy of R with the layout check and the skip rule (R50, R52).
7. Add the `line_item_count` check to the grader, and build the list of F9 invoices from the round 4 results.
8. Write `spe/evals/harness/r05-workflow.js` from the round 4 script. Remove P and add S.

### Gates, in order. Each gate must pass before the next one starts.

| Gate | Pass condition | On failure |
|---|---|---|
| Grader selftest | Every check, including the new `line_item_count`, passes its known-answer cases. The eval set hash matches round 4 (R54). | Halt and report a broken grader. |
| Control regrade | Regrading the round 4 outputs gives Q 0.93 and R 0.88 exactly (R55). | Halt and report. |
| Dry run | Q, R, and S each run on 3 invoices: one F9 two-column invoice, one scanned single-column invoice, and one clean single-column invoice. S skips cleanup only on the two-column invoice. The trace shows that S read no eval files (R52). | Fix the issue and run the dry run again. If the trace shows S read an eval file, halt and report a leaked answer key. |

### Launch

```js
{
  round: 5,
  configs: ["Q", "R", "S"],
  model: "Sonnet 5.5",
  invoices: 60,
  trialsPerInvoice: 1,
  predictions: "spe/predictions/r05.yaml",
  checks: ["field_accuracy_r04", "line_item_count"],
  outDir: "spe/evals/r05/"
}
```

### Cost estimate (not measured)

The full run is 3 configs × 60 invoices = 180 agent runs, plus 9 dry-run runs. That is the same config count as round 4, so cost and wall time should be close to round 4. I will halt and report if spend passes 1.5 times the round 4 spend.

### After the run

9. Make a local commit of the results with the subject `spe(r05): evaluate`.
10. Learn step: add the round 5 rows to `spe/prediction-log.md`. Mark F9 as fixed in `spe/failures.md` only if R51 passes. Log any new failure as F10 or later. Write "Proposed for round 6" in spec.md. Then make a local commit with the subject `spe(r05): learn`.

These commits stay local, and I will not push anything.
